ARSAP Overflow Area (FL165–FL235): activated under high EDWW FLG workload; when active, coordination and transfers of traffic through this area (instead of EDWW FLG ↔ EPWW D) take place directly between EDWW DBDS and EPWW D. FLG informs EPWW D of activation and deactivation.

IFR EDAH (RWY 10 departures and RWY 28 arrivals cross the DE/PL border): MRZ informs EPSC TWR of each IFR departure from RWY 10 before take-off clearance and of each IFR arrival to RWY 28 min. 5 min before IAF UDAXI. IFR traffic of EDAH crosses the border only on published procedures; EPSC TWR keeps its own traffic clear of them.
IFR via ALUKA: Bremen ACC provides separation between flights L619-ALUKA, GERGA DCT ABSAG DCT ALUKA and GILAS DCT RENKI.

Crossing EDUU airspace: when EDUU OSE/HVL is online, EPWW ACC requests a crossing release for departures from FIR EDWW with RFL above FL285 (traffic unknown to EDUU; the TopSky release works only in the upstream sector). Applies especially to EDDB departures via BODLA. Phrase: „Approval request for airspace crossing [callsign] inbound [waypoint].” Climb above FL280 only with EDUU approval when online; when EDUU is offline – no coordination needed, the TopSky release covers the upper and lower airspace.

Release = approval for the accepting unit to climb, descend and/or turn (max. 45°) before the transfer of control point; the transferring unit remains responsible for separation in its AoR unless agreed otherwise.
A VATSIM callsign in the LOA includes its variants (e.g. _X_CTR, _1_CTR) and higher positions taking over its duties (e.g. CTR for APP).
Coordination and transfer via the agreed COPs; coordinate deviations by voice, text or EuroScope coordination.
Transfer at the levels from the tables; when the RFL is lower – at the RFL if it causes no conflict, otherwise coordination. Situations not described – individual coordination between sectors.
After the transfer of communications no release for level changes and turns until the transfer of control, unless the LOA states otherwise.

Notation: ↓/↑ FLxxx – descending/climbing to FLxxx without further restrictions; FLxxxA – climbing and at or above FLxxx; FLxxxB – descending and at or below FLxxx; „at level” – level flight at an FL complying with the odd/even rule.

Hand-off: 1) the transferring sector sends the aircraft to the accepting frequency (by voice or text); 2) initiates the transfer in the radar client; 3) after the first call the accepting sector assumes the flight.
SSR: transfer on verified discrete codes or Mode-S A1000; code change by the accepting unit only after the transfer of control point.

Notation: ↓/↑ FLxxx – descending/climbing to FLxxx without further restrictions; FLxxxA – climbing and at or above FLxxx; FLxxxB – descending and at or below FLxxx; „at level” – level flight at an FL complying with the odd/even rule.

Hand-off: 1) the transferring sector sends the aircraft to the accepting frequency (by voice or text); 2) initiates the transfer in the radar client; 3) after the first call the accepting sector assumes the flight.
SSR: transfer on verified discrete codes; code change by the accepting unit only after the transfer of control point.

silent: Transfer of control at the AoR boundary.
Transfer of communications ESMM → EPWW: no later than the transfer of control point.
Transfer of communications EPWW → ESMM: no later than 20 NM before the AoR boundary.
Transfer of radar control after prior voice coordination – distance between aircraft not less than 5 NM.
Silent transfer of radar control: successive aircraft min. 10 NM, constant or increasing.
vfr: Controlled VFR: coordination, transfer of control and transfer of communications as IFR; uncontrolled VFR to the appropriate sector if in radio contact.
other: Release = approval for the accepting unit to climb, descend or turn (max. 45°) before the transfer of control.
Levels: standard allocation on all routes – in RVSM magnetic tracks 360°–179° odd, 180°–359° even.
Northbound overflights on L617 and M70 are one traffic flow; constant or increasing radar separation required, measured from KOLOB.
Northbound and north-westbound traffic released to ESMM for turns 20 NM before the AoR boundary, taking known traffic and active D areas into account.

General directs ESMM (without coordination; AoR boundary crossed min. 2.5 NM from the lateral boundary of both sectors, point in the FPL): ADES EPWA – SORIX, ADES EPGD – OGDAV. ESMM may also give a direct to any point in FIR EPWW if it is in the FPL.

General directs EPWW (same conditions): ESSA – ANFEV, NILUG; ESSB – ANFEV, INWIQ; ESKN – ANFEV, PELUP; EKCH, EKRK, ESMS – ROE; ESGG – NILEN; ENGM – XENTA, KSD; ENTO – REPKU. Other traffic to ESMM: EPWW or EPGD APP may give a direct GOSOT, KOLOB, GORPI, LUSID, PENOR, ROE if the point is in the FPL.
FRA: FIR Warszawa above FL95 excluding TMAs; DK-SE FAB above FL285, entry/exit points: AMROR, GORPI, GOSOT, KOLOB, LARMA, LUSID, PENOR, POKEN, RUMAR.
Delegation EPWW → ESMM (class C): MIDSEA FL95–FL460; RÖNNE SOUTH a FL195–FL460; RÖNNE SOUTH b FL245–FL460. Delegation ESMM → EPWW: not applicable.
Aircraft without 8.33 kHz: before the transfer of communications the transferring unit agrees the frequency with the accepting unit.
SSR: transfer on verified discrete codes or Mode-S A1000; code change by EPWW or EPGD APP only after the transfer of control point, by ESMM no earlier than 20 NM before the AoR boundary.
Mach number control: the pilot reports the assigned Mach to the accepting unit on first contact.
